previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, post-transplant graft-versus-host disease, systolic heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and near syncope at home. He was found to have acute on chronic heart failure with pulmonary edema and bilateral pleural effusions, leading to hypoxic respiratory failure. Treatment with intravenous furosemide improved his symptoms, though his renal function temporarily worsened, requiring careful management. His metabolic acidosis resolved, and imaging ruled out pulmonary embolism or infection. A non-contrast cardiac MRI showed severe left ventricular dysfunction without evidence of myocardial inflammation or iron overload. He was stabilized on home diuretics, with plans to initiate outpatient dialysis and follow-up with nephrology, cardiology, and pulmonology. He was discharged home with improved oxygenation and stable vital signs, continuing all baseline medications.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT ABD AND PELVIS W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ with prior perianal abscess, hypotension, abd  pain.  Post
incision and drainage of left perianal abscess in the ER today.  Evaluate for
abscess or other acute process.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT images of the abdomen and pelvis were acquired
without intravenous contrast. Non-contrast scan has several limitations in
detecting vascular and parenchymal organ abnormalities, including tumor
detection.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

No oral contrast was administered.

DOSE:   Total DLP (Body) = 1,257 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT pelvis from ___ and CT abdomen pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: There is bibasilar atelectasis but no pleural effusion or
pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic
or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  Surgical clips in the gallbladder fossa
denote prior cholecystectomy.

PANCREAS: The pancreas demonstrates mild atrophy, but otherwise normal
attenuation, without evidence of focal lesions or pancreatic ductal
dilatation. There is no peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen is enlarged to 14.9 cm, without focal lesion.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The bilateral kidneys are atrophic.  No renal stones identified. 
Very mild bilateral perinephric stranding is present.

GASTROINTESTINAL: Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber and wall
thickness throughout. Colon and rectum are within normal limits. Appendix is
normal in caliber without evidence of surrounding fat stranding. There is no
evidence of mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

RETROPERITONEUM: There is no evidence of retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: Slit-like IVC suggests volume depletion.  There is no abdominal
aortic aneurysm. There is mild to moderate calcium burden in the abdominal
aorta.  Of note, there is atherosclerotic calcification at the origin of the
celiac artery (2:25).

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

In the left perianal region, at the site of the previously described complex
fluid collection, a Malecot catheter drain is in place, with mild surrounding
soft tissue stranding.  There is no residual fluid collection.  The fat
stranding does not continue into the lower extremities.  No lower extremity
subcutaneous gas is identified.  A prominent, but not pathologically enlarged,
left perirectal lymph node is unchanged, and likely reactive (2:84).

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: Reproductive organs are within normal limits.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions. 
Multilevel degenerative changes of the lumbar spine are unchanged.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  A Malecot catheter drain is in place in the left perianal region, at the
site of the previously described perianal abscess.  There is no residual fluid
collection seen given noncontrast enhanced exam.  Adjacent soft tissue
stranding is identified, but it does not continue into the lower extremities. 
No soft tissue gas.

2.  Slit-like IVC suggests systemic volume depletion.

3.  Splenomegaly.
